title: Mushroom and trout hash with eggs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Potatoes, onion, mushrooms, trout, eggs, oil, thyme and lemon are all plain whole foods a grandparent would keep.

supermarket.reason: Trout fillets, mushrooms and the rest are everyday items at any big supermarket at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a large lidded frying pan and simple frying, steaming and egg-cracking that a beginner can manage.

works.reason: 800g potatoes steamed then fried, with mushrooms, two flaked trout fillets and four eggs, gives a sound, well-seasoned hash for four that will cook through as written.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes to cube the potatoes and slice the onion and mushrooms is fair, and the 15+10+5 minutes in the steps roughly match the 30 printed, with a few minutes extra for the eggs.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including thyme and lemon, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot mushroom hash with eggs suits a cold late-January morning, and the 300g of mushrooms is a main part of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Potatoes, mushrooms, onion, trout and eggs make a filling, balanced breakfast a family would happily eat again.
